parsed.explanation: Strong visitor-facing legal position: no criminalisation, foreign documents accepted, a 2024 equality law covering goods, services, healthcare and housing, in-force hate-speech protections, and demonstrated enforcement (21 arrests after the March 2024 mob attack; appellate conviction of three tourists for a 2017 assault). Courts and police act for trans victims. Counterweights: measurable social hostility above the regional norm (36% avoid locations for fear of assault vs 29%; only 35% open about being LGBTIQ), a serious 150-person mob attack on two trans people in 2024, dated (2013) police stopping/mistreatment of visibly trans people with complaints discontinued, and custody defaulting to registered sex with only an on-request transfer route (four detainees, one foreign, isolated before transfer). No border friction, no facility ban, no organised state targeting. Acceptance-with-working-remedy tier, held below 0.75 by documented societal hostility and the unresolved default custody rule.
